thread.title: Stocks Sell Off As Dow Loses 50-Day And Apple Falls Even Further

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Stocks Sell Off As Dow Loses 50-Day And Apple Falls Even Further
text:
Stock market index funds sold off Friday and fell below their 50-day moving average as Apple ( AAPL ) offset a big gain from General Electric ( GE ) in the Dow.
X PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) sank 1.6% in the stock market today , while SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) and SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) gave up 0.9% and 0.8%, respectively. Small caps fared somewhat better with iShares Russell 2000 ( IWM ) down 0.5%.
GE led the Dow with a jump of a nearly 4% after its quarterly results came in above views . Shares gapped up above their 50-day line as they try to recover from a long, steady decline.
Apple was the biggest blue chip loser, gapping below its 50-day line and dropping more than 4% in heavy trade. It's now testing support at its 200-day line. The stock had been working on the right side of a shallow base with a 183.60 buy point but is now back near the bottom of the pattern. Morgan Stanley trimmed its price target to 200 from 203, citing weaker iPhone sales .
Chip stocks have taken a beating recently. Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) on Thursday slumped 6% on its weak near-term guidance and cited weak smartphone demand, particularly at Apple, as one reason.
VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) and iShares PHLX Semiconductor ( SOXX ) were down about 1.2% each, following Thursday's big drops.
Consumer staples, gold miners and technology were among the biggest sector fund decliners. Gold futures dipped 0.8% to $1,338.40 an ounce.
Banks and telecom ETFs were among the few gainers. Bitcoin also rose. Prices were up 2.8% to $8,504.89, according to CoinDesk , near their intraday high. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) leapt nearly 9% to retake its 50-day line for the first time in three months.
Small Caps Shine Small caps have seemingly taken over where large caps left off, as many funds tracking the smaller-size segment of the market are near highs.
SPDR S&P 600 Small Value ( SLYV ) is one such fund. It's come back from its February lows and is now about 3% below its mid-January peak. The proper buy point would be 131.53, though the ETF could offer a slightly earlier entry at 129.42.
The $1.3 billion fund, which will turn 18 years old in September, provides access to the S&P SmallCap 600 Value Index. Stocks making the index exhibit value traits based on book-value-to-price ratio, earnings-to-price ratio and sales-to-price ratio. The weighted average market cap of the fund's holdings is about $1.7 billion.
Financials made up the biggest sector exposure as of Wednesday at 20% of assets. Industrials were next at 18.5%, consumer discretionary 15% and information technology 14%. Energy, materials and health care were the next biggest sectors, with weightings in the 6%-8% range.

Beating The S&P 500 SLYV's 2.7% year-to-date return through Wednesday is slightly ahead of the S&P 500, which is up 1.9%. The ETF's average annual returns over the past three and five years are nearly in line with the S&P index, though the fund widens the outperformance gap over the past 10 and 15 years. The small-cap fund bears a 0.15% expense ratio.
Another small-cap ETF nearing a potential buy point is iShares Russell 2000 Growth ( IWO ). It was featured in this ETF column on April 11, as shares regained their 50-day moving average .
Thursday's pick, PowerShares DWA Momentum Portfolio ( PDP ), remains close to a 55.87 buy point.
